articles.title: Chancellor rejects calls to raise Capital Gains Tax in Budget
articles.description: Influential Labour figures had been pushing for equalising CGT and income tax, but critics have said this could drive wealthy people out of Britain.
articles.summary: Chancellor John Healey says he wants to avoid an investor exodus from the UK Chancellor John Healey has dismissed calls from some Labour MPs to increase Capital Gains Tax (CGT).
key_points: Cabinet ministers Wes Streeting and Louise Haigh both previously voiced support for raising CGT before Andy Burnham became prime minister in July.
Ahead of next week's Budget, as first reported by the Times , external , Healey is minded not to increase CGT - which is imposed on the profit people make when they sell…
The move followed warnings that it could end up costing the government money if wealthy people leave the country or defer selling off assets.

articles.title: What is the Budget and what could be in it?
articles.description: Chancellor John Healey will set out his plans for UK taxes on 28 October.
articles.summary: Chancellor John Healey will set out Labour's tax and spending plans when he delivers his first Budget on 28 October.
key_points: He has refused to rule out tax increases after acknowledging government borrowing costs are at "historic highs".
Before the 2024 general election, Labour promised not to increase three big revenue earners for the government: income tax, National Insurance and VAT.
In his statement, delivered to MPs in the House of Commons, Healey will set out how the government plans to raise or lower taxes.

articles.title: Burnham vows end to 'rip-off parking charges' under new rules
articles.description: Penalties are seen as too harsh on motorists who are penalised for parking on private land.
articles.summary: Drivers will be given the right to challenge "rip off" private parking charges and more grace when using private providers under new rules set out by Andy Burnham.
key_points: The Prime Minister announced the changes after drivers repeatedly raised concerns penalties issued by private providers were too harsh and left motorists unfairly penalised.
In one case, a woman was taken to court in a £1,906 claim after taking longer than five minutes to pay at a car park in Derby .

Private car parks already have an industry code of practice, but the RAC motoring group said the government's changes would protect drivers from the "poor practices of some private parking companies".

key_points: Vacancies fell by 21,000 in the three months to September to 691,000, according to the Office for National Statistics (ONS), which said small firms were citing labour costs as a key factor in…
Energy costs have risen since the Iran war began, and companies have also said that increases in National Insurance and the minimum wage have made it more expensive to employ staff.
The ONS figures also showed the unemployment rate fell to 4.7% in the three months to August, the lowest for more than a year.

articles.title: UK beef, lamb, pork and dairy production to fall in 2027
articles.summary: The Agriculture and Horticulture Development Board (AHDB) has said that constrained cattle and sheep supply will remain a key feature of the market, underpinning market fundamentals in the years ahead.
key_points: Across the board, the levy body is expecting production of beef, lamb, pork and dairy to fall over the next year.

UK beef production, for example, is set to fall to 896,000 tonnes in 2027, marking a year-on-year decline of 0.8%, with increased carcass weights expected to only partially offset lower cattle throughputs.
The outlook for sheep is little better, with production forecast to decline by 2.4% to 262,000 tonnes in 2027 due to lower slaughter numbers and a contracting breeding flock.

Specifically, this action also applies to bivalve molluscs, including clams and oysters, but not crab or finfish, also known as “true fish”.

articles.title: AI-Enabled FP&A Orchestration: Evolution, Gaps & Pathways
articles.summary: When you watch a symphony orchestra, you can see the conductor, the musicians and the instruments, but what is really magical is the invisible architecture that keeps them together: coordination.FP&A is just the same.
key_points: The conductor is FP&A itself: setting direction, owning the decision, and remaining accountable for the outcome.
The musicians are our analysts and finance teams: providing the judgement and business context that no system can ever replace.
The instruments are our AI agents and data systems: continuous, scalable, and built to run in parallel.Every great performance relies on a hidden layer of coordination.

articles.title: Measuring the Invisible: How CFOs Must Evaluate FP&A Talent in an AI-First Function — Part 3 of 3
articles.summary: Why output metrics fail in agentic finance — and what to measure instead.In Parts 1 and 2, I argued that agentic AI does not shrink the FP&A role so much as relocate it [1] [2].
key_points: The routine production of a variance pack or a driver-based forecast moves to the agent; what remains for the professional is judgment in the probabilistic zone that the agent cannot be trusted to…
Part 1 set out the capability that judgment requires — the FP&A Agent Manager and a four-layer stack: Data & Tooling Literacy, Probabilistic Model Behaviour, Probability Theory, Control Design.
Part 2 addressed how to build the pipeline that produces those people through the GROOM framework.Both described the capability and how to grow it.
